title: Advanced VFX
objective: Select an advanced VFX route, prepare compatible references, generate one video transformation test, and review what changed, what stayed stable, and the first correction.
submission: Record the selected workflow, source and reference assets, tool and mode, working prompt, result link, review notes and first correction in the official Homework Doc. Follow current cohort instructions for sharing or presenting the result; the supplied source gives no separate submission destination or deadline.

steps.title: Choose one transformation and a base shot
steps.instruction: Select one effect the available footage can support: object replacement, character and scene transformation, full scene redesign, motion transfer, character replacement, or reference-to-video. Identify the original clip and state what must change and what should remain stable before opening a generation tool.
steps.review: The chosen effect is specific, the base shot is identified, and the intended change is separated from details that should be preserved.

steps.title: Prepare the reference set
steps.instruction: Capture a useful frame when the source describes a screenshot workflow. Prepare only the references required by your route: subject, prop, costume, background, plain matte or other named elements. If using the reference-to-video route, the source demonstrates removing a subject from a frame, using the clip to ask Gemini for a prompt with explicit reference anchors, and attaching the prepared elements in Vidu Q2.
steps.review: Every reference has a clear role and agrees with the requested subject, scene, framing and motion.

steps.title: Choose the video method for the transformation
steps.instruction: Match the method to the job. The source pairs object replacement with Kling 1 Video-to-Video, a boxing scene with OpenArt video-to-video and Kling 3.0, scene replacement with Seedance 2.0, motion transfer with OpenArt Motion Sync and DreamActor M2.0 or Kling 3.0, character replacement with OpenArt Replace Body or Kling 01, and element-based reference-to-video with Vidu Q2. Treat the reported winners and issues as class observations rather than guarantees.
steps.review: The selected method supports the intended transformation and uses the references that method expects.

steps.title: Generate one test and inspect the full clip
steps.instruction: Use the closest complete source prompt or adapt a working copy for your own footage. Keep the transformation request focused and name the details the source says to preserve, such as face, body motion, timing, camera position, lighting, background or props. Review the clip from beginning to end instead of judging only its strongest frame.
steps.review: The test applies the requested change while retaining the selected identity, movement, timing and framing constraints.

steps.title: Record the result and the first correction
steps.instruction: Compare the generated clip with the source. Note changes that worked, any identity or scene drift, lighting or relighting problems, unstable props, unwanted background changes, and motion that no longer matches. Save the selected clip and its source/reference links in the Homework Doc, then state the first correction supported by what you observed.
steps.review: A result link, selected method, source/reference links, review notes and evidence-based first correction are recorded.

homework.title: Choose and scope one effect
homework.prompt: Choose one demonstrated VFX use case that fits footage you can access. Record the base shot, the intended transformation, the details that must stay stable, and why the selected route fits the material.

homework.title: Prepare a compatible reference set
homework.prompt: Gather and label the source video or screenshot and the subject, prop, costume, character, matte, or background references needed for your selected route. Record what each asset should control and check that the references do not conflict.

homework.title: Run one video transformation test
homework.prompt: Select a source-backed tool and mode for the transformation, make a working prompt from the supplied prompt packet, attach the correct references, and generate a test. Record the exact tool, model, mode, inputs, and prompt version you used.

homework.title: Review the full result and choose a first fix
homework.prompt: Compare the result with the source across identity, movement, timing, camera, lighting, scene, props, and unwanted changes. Save a link to the selected output, describe one observed problem, and record the first correction that addresses that evidence.

prompts.title: Sample Vidu Q2 elements-to-video prompt
prompts.text:
Generate a cinematic action sequence combining the environment of [background_image_ref] with the exact subject from [character_image_ref], strictly adhering to the motion, timing, and framing of [screen_grab_ref]. 
Setting: A dramatic night scene filled with thick, atmospheric smoke and dust. The background features an old, gothic stone church structure outlined by draped strings of glowing yellow fairy lights. The dusty ground is scattered with distinct, intense pools of burning fire. The ambient lighting is warm, driven by flickering orange and yellow firelight against the dark night.
Character: The subject is an Indian man strictly matching [character_image_ref]—it is crucial that his facial features, specifically his clear aviator glasses, mustache, and goatee, remain consistent without morphing. He wears a highly detailed, tactical full-body red armor suit with raised muscle panels, glowing red-orange light strips, and a metallic gold "E" emblem on the chest.
Action & Camera: The scene begins dynamically as the character drops rapidly down from out of frame. He lands heavily in the center of the frame in a deep, bent-knee crouch, kicking up a cloud of dust on impact. From this crouch, he immediately rises and squares his shoulders directly to the camera, entering a tense, wide-legged power stance with arms slightly flared out. Once fully standing and front-facing, he aggressively uses his hands to pull a red cloth mask up to cover his mouth and nose, locking his eyes into an intense, piercing stare directly at the lens. The camera executes a smooth, continuous dolly-in (pushing forward) throughout the entire sequence, closing in on his face and upper body as the ground fires continuously burn around him.
prompts.source: AI VFX USE CASES, Prompt sample for Vidu Q2 Elements to Video; supplied Google Doc

quiz.question: For the candle replacement, what does the source prompt explicitly ask the video model to preserve?
options: The original video apart from the candle transformation and glow.
Only the first frame; the other movement can be replaced.
The actor's motion should stop while the background changes.
quiz.explanation: The supplied prompt says to make no changes to the original video other than the candle glowing.

quiz.question: When you use separate elements for Vidu Q2, what should the prompt describe accurately?
options: The character image alone, without motion or framing.
The scene, subject, motion, timing and framing, with explicit reference anchors.
A new shot that ignores the screen grab.
quiz.explanation: The source asks Gemini for a faithful clip description and reference anchors, then the sample prompt assigns the background, character and screen-grab references distinct roles.

quiz.question: A scene change alters a face or camera position that should stay fixed. What is the most useful first review?
options: Check that the prompt and reference clearly identify the face and camera details to preserve.
Add unrelated scene references to make the prompt more complex.
Treat the changed face as proof the effect is complete.
quiz.explanation: The source prompts repeatedly call out facial features, body position and camera framing as constraints for scene changes.

quiz.question: How should you choose between the demonstrated video methods?
options: Use one model for every effect, regardless of the inputs.
Match the method to the change and references, then review its result and limitations.
Choose only from the class-reported winner labels.
quiz.explanation: The source demonstrates different tools for object replacement, scene redesign, motion transfer, character replacement and elements-to-video. Its reported winners are class observations, not guarantees.
